apps/server/src/serverSettings.ts.why: Every settings write goes through upstream's patch and write paths here. The fork swaps in its patch (fork/serverSettingsPatch.ts, under upstream's name, so a project's MCP profile a client left out is kept) and calls its save check (fork/serverSettingsWriteCheck.ts) once in each write path. The load decodes the file in fork/settingsFileRead.ts (old auto-update names renamed, an unusable interval left out so it reads as its default), in the server's fiber so what a lenient field drops is logged to the server's logger (#975); upstream's private settings schema is decoded there through the one exported decodePersistedSettings, which the fork report and the Claude MCP profile reader also pass to the silent copy of that decode. The lines from "import { renameRetiredAutoUpdateKeys }" on predate this list (#277): the load's decode of the file, which the fork report shares and which needs upstream's private decoders here, and the fallback when the file cannot be read. When the file fails to load, upstream runs on its defaults, whose model policy is off; the fork reads the policy from the file on its own and fails closed (enforce, nothing allowed) when the file does not parse, so a broken file never turns an enforced policy off (fork/modelPolicyFile.ts, #731). Each listed copy is one the fork adds over upstream; the run from upstream refuses a spare one (#311). Since v0.1.14 upstream decodes the file in its own pure decodeSettingsFile(): it reads through the fork's silent decode (decodeSettingsFileSilently, one changed line), and the load runs the fork's logSettingsFileRead() first, in its fiber, for the warnings; the fork's fallback values (automaticUpdates off, the model policy) are in upstream's fallback there.

apps/server/src/peer/RemoteDelegation.ts.why: #386: a remote delegate_task interrupted after its launch there (the parent's turn moved on) still records and follows its task: the launch, record and follow run as one uninterruptible step. A launch recorded with no task here is stopped there with a warning, as a failed record is. Tested in apps/server/src/fork/remoteDelegationAbortSafe.test.ts. Upstream PR pingdotgg/t3code#30249 (record before launch) rewrites this block, and its intent differs: after an interrupted, uncertain launch it stops the child there, while this seam keeps the child and follows it. Whoever brings #30249 in through fork-follow must choose on purpose between stopping and keeping (and expect a merge conflict on this block), then drop this seam or keep it. Also #386: lastReply reads a task's reply through fork/remoteReplyRead.ts, which decodes the answer again without the thread's details when the full read does not decode, so a linked environment on another version (thread details missing a field this version requires) still delivers the reply. Tested in apps/server/src/fork/remoteReplyRead.test.ts. Also #532: a remote delegate_task carries its parent's resolved MCP profile in delegatedFrom (fork/remoteMcpProfile.ts), worked out before the uninterruptible launch so a refusal or an interrupt sends nothing; a profile narrower than all goes only to an environment whose GET /api/fork/features (fork/forkFeatures.ts, answered only to its link token) says mcpProfileCarry, and only to an instance there whose driver applies one (Claude; #661 asks that environment's orchestrator_capabilities for the launch's instance). Tested in apps/server/src/fork/remoteMcpProfile.test.ts. MCP profiles PR 6 (#875): the carry also gets the call's input, so a delegate_task to another machine that names a narrower `mcpProfile` carries that profile (checked within the parent's) instead of the parent's.

scripts/prepare-server-compile-cache.cjs.why: #514: the macOS x64 build warms the server compile cache by running the x64 engine under Rosetta. Upstream's 120 s limit for that step fits its 12-core Mac runner, but on the fork's 3-core GitHub runner it took 116 s once and ran over once, failing the release. The fork's lines wrap the hook's own spawnSync with scripts/fork-cache-timeout.cjs, which raises a shorter limit to 360 s only when the step runs under Rosetta (no other target; a longer upstream limit is kept), and shadow spawnSync with it in the try block, so upstream's call line is unchanged. Tested in scripts/fork-cache-timeout.test.ts. Drop this seam when the fork builds macOS x64 on a bigger runner or upstream's limit is 360 s or more.

scripts/build-desktop-artifact.ts.why: #822: without signing secrets electron-builder finds no identity and signs nothing, so the shipped macOS app keeps only the linker signature of Electron's own executable, which seals none of the renamed bundle, and `codesign --verify --deep --strict` fails on it ("code has no resources but signature indicates they must be present"). For an unsigned build the fork's line sets identity "-" and the sign hook scripts/fork-codesign.cjs, which runs `codesign --force --deep --sign -` as electron-builder's last change to the bundle, before the zip and dmg are made from it. Signed builds keep upstream's line and scripts/sign-macos.ts. fork-release.yml's verify_mac_signature job checks the app in each shipped zip and dmg. Tested in scripts/fork-codesign.test.ts. Drop this seam when upstream ad-hoc signs unsigned macOS builds, or when the fork signs with a Developer ID (#803).

A save records the MCP profile of the thread that made it, and refuses a narrower thread's change that would let the task's runs get more than its own profile; a run that starts a new thread is refused when that thread would get more than the recorded profile (fork/scheduledTaskMcpProfile.ts, #699). The stored-delivery worker names its own delivery to keepStored, and a delivery it removes before its run (payload not prepared, prompt too long) leaves its place in line at once rather than at the sweep (fork/agentSlotRoutes.ts, #941).

//pending: Upstream files whose fork lines predate counting every upstream file, each with its ceiling: the most fork lines it may hold against upstream (counted from upstream, as fork-follow runs the check). To move into fork files or pin as seams; lower a ceiling when lines move out and take a file off when none are left. A pull request may change them but not grow them.
//forkFiles: Files upstream does not have that are not named as fork files (a fork, fork-*, forkName or FORK_* folder or file). A pull request's run, which has no upstream commit, takes them for the fork's own. dir/ is everything under it, ** any folders, * any characters but /, !path never. A pattern that matches an upstream file fails the check from upstream.
//lost: Seam and pending files that lost upstream lines, counted from upstream (as fork-follow runs the check): "lines", the upstream lines not kept in order and indentation; "gone", those whose text is gone. Held exactly, like a ceiling; an unlisted file counts 0. Lower a count when a line comes back, and keep each one small: a count is not a set of lines, so a line counted here may move unseen, and in a pending file a pull request can put back one gone upstream line and delete another with both counts unchanged.
